Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

**Translate these to a dedicated tool instead:**
- `cat` / `head` / `tail` (known path) → `Read`
- `sed` / `awk` (in-place edit) → `Edit`
- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")
- Compose multi-step logic in a single call with `if` / `case` / `for` / `while` control flows.
- Do not set `run_in_background=true`; background task management tools are not available.

**Commands available:**
The following common command categories are usually available. Availability still depends on the host, so when in doubt run `which <command>` first to confirm a command exists before relying on it.
- Navigation and inspection: `ls`, `pwd`, `cd`, `stat`, `file`, `du`, `df`, `tree`
- File and directory management: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `ln`, `chmod`, `chown`
- Text and data processing: `wc`, `sort`, `uniq`, `cut`, `tr`, `diff`, `xargs`
- Archives and compression: `tar`, `gzip`, `gunzip`, `zip`, `unzip`
- Networking and transfer: `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `ssh`, `scp`
- Version control: `git`; for GitHub-hosted work (PRs, issues, CI runs, API queries) prefer the `gh` CLI when installed — it carries the user's GitHub auth and can return structured JSON
- Process and system: `ps`, `kill`, `top`, `env`, `date`, `uname`, `whoami`
- Language and package toolchains: `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `python`, `pip` (use whichever the project actually relies on)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. tools.description:
Read a text file from the local filesystem.

If the user provides a concrete file path to a text file, call Read directly. Do not `Glob`, `ls`, or otherwise pre-check known text file paths; missing or invalid file paths return errors you can handle. Do not use Read for directories; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob when you need files matching a name pattern (Glob lists files only, never directories). When you need several files, prefer to read them in parallel: emit multiple `Read` calls in a single response instead of reading one file per turn.

- Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.
- Returns up to 1000 lines or 100 KB per call, whichever comes first; lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated mid-line.
- Page larger files with `line_offset` (1-based start line) and `n_lines`. Omit `n_lines` to read up to the 1000-line cap.

- Negative line_offset reads from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines); the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.

# 08 — Date format, filename generation/parsing, calendar & year navigation

Probed black-box on `/workspace/executable` (version banner: `commit-93cc85d16ab60ba8d646458fe0233778317b22a3`).
System date during probing: **Sat 2026-08-08 (UTC)**. HOME=/opt/uiuc-agent/home.
All TUI runs used the pty harness; log creation used `EDITOR=<script that appends "X\n">`.

## 0. TUI basics needed to reproduce anything

- Initial keyboard focus is on the **Sections menu**, NOT the calendar. Focus order with `Tab`:
  Sections → Tags → Calendar. The focused menu's selected row is drawn inverted (`\x1b[7m`).
  Until the calendar is focused, `hjkl`/arrows/Enter do nothing to dates.
- `+` / `-` (year nav) work from ANY focus (global keys).
- `q` quits (exit 0). The TUI ignores SIGTERM.
- At startup only `<log-dir>/scratchpads/` is created. `y<year>/` is created lazily the first
  time a log is opened for that year (the dir stays even if the file ends up deleted).

## 1. Filename generation (what file is created for a date)

Config key is `log-filename-format` (README name). CLI flag is `--log-name-format` (note:
**name**, not "filename"; the help text has no defaults printed). CLI overrides config.
CLI `--log-name-format` and config `log-filename-format` both confirmed working.

**The compiled-in default is NOT the README's `d%y_%m_%d.md`.** With no option, opening
today's log creates `<log-dir>/y2026/d2026_08_08.md` (4-digit year), so the real default
behaves like `d%Y_%m_%d.md`. Passing `d%y_%m_%d.md` explicitly yields `d26_08_08.md`.

Observed generations for date 2026-08-08 (format → file created under `y2026/`):

| format | created file |
|---|---|
| (default) | `d2026_08_08.md` |
| `d%y_%m_%d.md` | `d26_08_08.md` |
| `%Y_%m_%d.md` | `2026_08_08.md` |
| `%y-%m-%d.md` | `26-08-08.md` |
| `%m.md` | `08.md` |
| `%d.md` | `08.md` |
| `%e.md` | `␣8.md` (space-padded day) |
| `%B.md` | `August.md` |
| `%b.md` | `Aug.md` |
| `%H.md` | `00.md` (time fields are always 0) |
| `%p_%I.md` | `AM_12.md` |
| `%j.md` | `001.md` (day-of-year is NOT computed; tm_yday stays 0) |
| `%A.md` | `Sunday.md` (weekday NOT computed; tm_wday stays 0 — 2026-08-08 is actually Saturday) |
| `%a_%w.md` | `Sun_0.md` |
| `%F.md` | `2026-08-08.md` (composites of Y/m/d work) |
| `a%%b.md` | `a%b.md` |
| `plain.md` | `plain.md` (no specifiers → constant name) |
| `%Q.md` | `%Q.md` (unknown specifiers pass through literally, NO error) |
| `x%.md` | `x%.md` (trailing `%` stays literal, NO error) |
| `d%y_%m_%d_%Q.md` | `d26_08_08_%Q.md` |
| `%m/%d.md` | `y2026/08/08.md` — slashes in the format create nested subdirs |

Conclusion: generation is a plain strftime over a `struct tm` that has ONLY
year/month/mday populated (wday, yday, hour, min, sec all zero). Everything strftime
accepts "works"; unknown/convenience specifiers behave per libc.

### Empty format is the only rejected format

`--log-name-format ''` (or empty config value) aborts at startup, before any directory
is created (not even `scratchpads/`), printing to stdout (exit code 1):

```
Captain's log encountered an error:

```

Exact bytes (piped): `Captain's log encountered an error: \n Log filename format can not be empty!\n\t`
— note the space after `error: `, the leading space before `Log`, and a trailing TAB after `!`.

## 2. The log file lifecycle (Enter on a date)

1. App ensures `y<year>/` exists, creates `<log-dir>/y<YYYY>/<formatted-name>` with the
   template content, then runs `$EDITOR <path>` (via shell).
2. Template content for date DD.MM.YY is exactly 12 bytes, **no trailing newline**:
   `# 08. 08. 26.` — i.e. `# %d. %m. %y.` (2-digit year!). Verified for today
   (`# 08. 08. 26.`), for 2027-08-08 (`# 08. 08. 27.`), and single-digit day
   (`# 03. 08. 26.` — zero-padded).
3. After the editor exits, **if the file content is byte-identical to the template, the
   file is deleted** (this is content comparison, not mtime: rewriting the same bytes or
   `touch`ing the file still deletes it). `EDITOR=/bin/true` therefore leaves no file.
   If the editor changed anything (e.g. appended one byte), the file is kept.
4. The `There are N log entries...` counter and calendar highlight update live after
   returning from the editor.

## 3. Parsing back / which files count as log entries (TUI)

Top bar right segment: `There are N log entries for year X.` (no singular form:
`There are 1 log entries for year 2024.`). It updates when the displayed year changes
and live when a log is created.

Behaviorally, the count for displayed year X is: **the number of days of year X whose
format-generated filename exists inside `<log-dir>/yX/`**. Evidence:

- `y2026/d2026_08_01.md`, `y2026/d2026_08_02.md` → count 2.
- A **0-byte** file with a valid generated name counts.
- Files in the log **root** (`logs/d2026_08_03.md`) do NOT count — only `y<year>/` subdirs.
- `scratchpads/`, arbitrary subdirs (`randomdir/`), nested dirs (`y2026/nested/`), and
  non-conforming dir names (`y26/`, `y2026x/`) are NOT scanned for the year views.
- `y2025/d2026_08_07.md` (dir/name year mismatch) counts for NEITHER year (0 in 2025
  view, 0 in 2026 view). Conversely `y2026/d2025_05_05.md` does not count for 2026.
- Impossible generated names never count: `d2026_13_01.md`, `d2026_02_29.md` (2026 not
  a leap year; `y2024/d2024_02_29.md` DOES count), `d2026_04_31.md`, `d2026_00_10.md`,
  `d2026_05_00.md`, `d2026_08_32.md` — all excluded.
- `d2026_8_04.md` (single-digit month) does NOT count with the default format — the
  generated name is `d2026_08_04.md`, which simply doesn't exist.
- With format `plain.md`: one existing file `y2026/plain.md` → **365** entries for 2026
  (every day of the non-leap year generates that name).
- With format `%m.md` and file `y2026/08.md` → **31** entries (all days of August).
- With format `%d.md` and file `y2026/08.md` → **12** entries (the 8th of every month).

(single-digit month) never appears; the same tag in `y2026/d2026_08_04.md` appears.
(Aside: section/tag titles are displayed lowercased in the menus: `# Sec` shows as `sec`.)

Highlighted dates: a date with an existing log file is rendered **underlined**
(`\x1b[4m`). Today's date is red (`\x1b[31m`), weekend columns are blue (`\x1b[34m`),

### The `--encrypt/--decrypt` path uses a real (lenient) parser instead

`--encrypt --password test` prints `Applying crypto...` (exit 0) and encrypts IN PLACE
every file under `y<dir>/` **and** `scratchpads/` whose ENTIRE name matches the filename
format parsed strptime-style:

- Encrypted: `d2026_08_01.md`, `d2026_8_04.md`, `d2026_1_5.md` (**single-digit month and
  day ARE accepted here**), `d2026_02_30.md` (Feb 30 accepted — no per-month day check),

- NOT encrypted: `d2026_13_01.md` (month 13), `d2026_08_32.md` (day 32), `d2026_08_00.md`,
